## GH-32 — universal F-port dichotomy, not just finite observations

Let p=8m+3>=11 be prime, n=2m=(p-3)/4. Let
\[
F_m(z)=\sum_{r=0}^m \frac{(-m)_r^2}{(2m+2)_r\,r!}z^r,\qquad D_m=\binom{3m+1}{m}\in\mathbb F_p^\times.
\]
By previously proved GH-28, for \(\vartheta^2=2\) in \(\mathbb F_{p^2}\), \(t=2\vartheta/3\),
\[
D_m F_m(9)=9^m P_n(t)\quad(\bmod p). \tag{1}
\]
Because p=3 mod8, \(\vartheta^p=-\vartheta\). Because n is even, the Legendre value is in \(\mathbb F_p\).

**Theorem:** For every such p,
\[
\boxed{F_m(9)=0\iff\left(\frac{-6}{p}\right)=-1\iff p\equiv19\pmod{24}.} \tag{2}
\]
In the remaining class p=11 mod24, F_m(9) is nonzero.

**Exact character-polynomial bridge.** For an indeterminate T put
\[
a(T)=-\tfrac32(3T+5),\quad b(T)=-9T-7,\quad
\mathsf H_p(T)=[X^{p-1}](X^3+a(T)X+b(T))^{(p-1)/2}. \tag{3}
\]
Zhi-Hong Sun, Congruences concerning Legendre polynomials II (arXiv:1012.3898), proves for T in \(\mathbb F_p\)
\[
P_{\lfloor p/4\rfloor}(T)=-
\left(\frac{-6}{p}\right)\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p}
\left(\frac{x^3+a(T)x+b(T)}{p}\right). \tag{4}
\]
Euler's criterion and the complete finite-field power sum show the sum in (4) equals \(-\mathsf H_p(T)\): the X-degree \(3(p-1)/2\) is below \(2(p-1)\), and only the positive exponent p-1 survives the sum. Thus \(P_n(T)=(-6/p)\mathsf H_p(T)\) at each T in \(\mathbb F_p\).

This equality extends as **polynomials over \(\mathbb F_p[T]\)**. Indeed write \(r=(p-1)/2=2n+1\). A monomial contributing to the coefficient of \(X^{p-1}=X^{4n+2}\) has \(3i+j=4n+2\), \(i+j+\ell=2n+1\). Therefore i>=n+1 and its T-degree is <=j+ell=2n+1-i<=n. Both \(\mathsf H_p(T)\) and \(P_n(T)\) have degree <=n<p. Equality at all p points proves polynomial identity, so it also holds at the non-rational quadratic point \(t=2\vartheta/3\):
\[
\boxed{P_n(t)=\left(\frac{-6}{p}\right)\mathsf H_p(t).} \tag{5}
\]
No quadratic character was illegitimately extended from \(\mathbb F_p\) to \(\mathbb F_{p^2}\).

**CM curve and Deuring.** Over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)\), specialize (3) at \(T=2\sqrt2/3\):
\[
E_*:\quad Y^2=X^3-\tfrac32(5+2\sqrt2)X-(7+6\sqrt2). \tag{6}
\]
Exact rational algebra gives
\[
4a^3+27b^2=\tfrac{27}{2}(2\sqrt2-3),\quad
\Delta(E_*)=-216(2\sqrt2-3),\quad
\boxed{j(E_*)=2417472+1707264\sqrt2}. \tag{7}
\]
The factor \(2\sqrt2-3\) has norm 1. Thus (6) has good reduction at all primes p>3. The j-invariant is a root of the known Hilbert class polynomial
\[
H_{-24}(J)=J^2-4834944J+14670139392
\]
of the maximal order of \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-6})\). E_* has CM by that order over the algebraic closure. By Deuring's reduction criterion, at every p>3 it is supersingular iff p is inert in K, i.e. \((-6/p)=-1\), and ordinary iff \((-6/p)=+1\). The coefficient \(\mathsf H_p(t)\) in (3) is the elliptic Hasse invariant, zero exactly for supersingular reduction. Equations (1) and (5), together with p-units D_m and 9, prove (2). In the class p=3 mod8, \((-6/p)\) is -1 for 19 mod24 and +1 for 11 mod24. QED.

The **new CM E_*** is not the GH-25/GH-31 non-CM elliptic curve \(y^2=x(x+1)(9x+1)\), whose \(j=4\cdot73^3/81\). Its exact mod-p observer certifies the GH-28 F total; it does **not** recover the distinct weighted G square-fiber residue or native six-dimensional X6 state.

## GH-33 — unconditional elimination of the second-order Laurent obstruction

For every p=19 mod24, GH-32 gives F_m(9)=0. The already proved GH-18 squarefreeness and coprimality, with \(G_m(z)=16zF_m'(z)+5F_m(z)\), imply \(F_m'(9)\ne0\) and \(G_m(9)=144F_m'(9)\ne0\). By GH-17,
\[
\boxed{\mathcal H_d(9)=0,\qquad\mathcal H_d'(9)\ne0},
\quad d=2m,\quad\mathcal H_d(z)=F_m(z)G_m(z). \tag{8}
\]
The Laurent obstruction \(\mathcal H_d\) differs from elliptic Hasse \(\mathsf H_p\).

GH-16's double-pole coefficient \(A_0=\alpha_p 9^{2d+2}\mathcal H_d(9)/(9-1)\) now vanishes for **all** target primes. GH-15's exact transport gives \(A_r=0\) at every authentic truncated rank \(0\le r\le d\), so the cyclic Gosper resolvent has poles of order at most one. Its original-endpoint-preserving finite formula becomes
\[
\boxed{T_{p,9}=C_d(H_d+8d+1)-H_0+B_0 L\quad(\bmod p).} \tag{9}
\]
Here \(H_r\) are GH-15 Laurent finite parts; \(B_0\) is a Laurent simple-pole residue, NOT the original Hasse B0; \(L=\sum_{r<d}\ell_r\) is the genuine first-logarithmic transfer moment. Equation (9) does NOT assert \(T_{p,9}=0\); cancellation of its remaining components is the next exact theorem obligation. The class-11 G_m(9)=0 claim also remains open.

## Evidence, provenance, BRC, continuation

Companion pure-Python standard-library checker was executed with exact arithmetic: 253 (p,T) point checks of Sun's polynomial identity (p=7,11,19,23,43,67,83), plus independent Hasse coefficient over \(\mathbb F_{p^2}\), Legendre recurrence, terminating F_m and GH-28 bridge for **all 76 primes** p<2001 with p=3 mod8. It passed: class19 zeros 37/37, class11 nonzeros 39/39. Symbolic exact algebra separately verified the discriminant, j, and Hilbert polynomial root. Finite tests supplement, not replace, published Sun, CM class polynomial and Deuring inputs.

Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.3898 (Sun's theorem); https://numberdb.org/Hilbert_class_polynomials (entry -24); https://mathoverflow.net/questions/18591/reduction-of-cm-elliptic-curves (Deuring criterion with Lang attribution).
